description: A man in a pressed shirt with a lanyard he has never been asked for, holding a clipboard against his chest like a shield. He has the specific alertness of somebody who's always four minutes from a problem, and the resting face of somebody who has already solved it and been thanked by nobody.

billing.text: "That was mine," he says. "My idea. I thought it read as clean. Drop the name, drop the ego, just PRODUCER, like the old shows." He looks at the middle distance for slightly too long. "Turns out a word can't be thanked. A word can't be hired by somebody else. I had a name and I gave it away for a font."

options.label: So you got rid of him.

building.text: "He did." Phil says it straight away, with no argument in it at all. "After the marriage went, Neil was on sofas the better part of a year, and one of those sofas was Nguyen's. Basement flat under a laundromat. I have never said otherwise and I never will." He turns a page over. "You're standing in it, by the way."

options.label: I'll ask you again after a good one.

change.text: "I could." The clipboard comes back up between you. "Ask me again after a good one."

dq_recruited.text:
He reads the brochure. Then he reads it again, slower, the way you read something that has your own name in it.

"I've had this lanyard eleven years," he says. "Nobody has asked to see it. Not once. Not security, not the desk, nobody." He touches it. "I kept turning up because I couldn't work out how to stop turning up."

He folds the brochure into a pocket that already has a pen in it.

"Tell Corliss yes. Tell him I said yes properly, out loud, with a witness, because I want it to have happened."

else.text: "I could produce something else," he agrees, pleasantly. "Nothing else in this city goes out live at eight o'clock with a man who genuinely doesn't know what he's about to say." A small, real shrug. "I like the not knowing. It's the only part of my week that isn't a schedule."

options.label: That's a hard way to treat the man who housed him.

gotrid.text: "I made it uncomfortable," he says, and doesn't dress it up. "I put things in front of Neil at the right hours. I let a couple of arguments run that I could have cut. Nothing I said was untrue. That's the part I'd want you to check. I just chose the ten minutes." He puts the clipboard down for the first time. "And then the credits rolled and there it was. Producer, Captain Nguyen. Still there. Nineteen weeks after he stopped coming down the stairs."

options.label: You have had a lot of time to think about how you say it.

hard.text: "It is," Phil agrees, without defending it. "He's not a bad man. I want to be accurate, because I have had a lot of time to think about how I say this." A pause. "He gave a man a bed. I run a programme. Those are two different kinds of good and only one of them fits in half an hour."

knows.text: "He knows it at four in the afternoon," Phil says. "By eight he's a genius who invented television. That's not a criticism. That's the job description. You can't do what he does at eight if you believe what he believes at four."

neil.text: "He's worse when he's trying to be good," Phil says. "The nights he behaves, nobody watches. The nights he goes off about his wife's pans for six minutes, the meter moves." He checks the stairs. "I've stopped deciding which of those I want. I just make sure the transmitter's warm."

nevertook.text: "Neil doesn't edit," Phil says. "Neil accretes." He picks the clipboard back up. "So I won, and the man I beat is still in the credits, and I'm a word. If you're looking for the moral of the programme, that's nearer than anything Neil says on it."

options.label: So you got rid of him.
He put Neil up, though. Back when he had nowhere.

nguyen.text: "He was a lovely man and he was killing us," Phil says. "He wasn't crew. He wasn't staff. He wasn't anything at all. He was a bloke Neil used to go out with, back when Neil went out. And he sold a root out of his trousers on my air, and Neil gave him a producer credit for it because Neil gives everybody everything at eleven o'clock at night."

root.first: "You're not crew," he says, not unkindly, checking a clipboard he doesn't need to check. "Doesn't matter. Nobody's crew. I'm Phil. I produce the programme, which tonight means I'm the programme's entire crew, its legal department and its cleaner." He offers a hand. "Don't touch the board."

options.label: Why does it say PRODUCER in the credits and not your name?
"Phil. Have you ever thought about ownership?"
options.text: "Phil. Have you ever thought about ownership?"

root.text: "We're up in about an hour," he says, without checking anything. "Or we're up whenever he comes down the stairs. Those are the two schedules."

text_by_relation.familiar: "Good, you're here." He hands you a page. "Hold that. If he asks what it is, it's the running order. It isn't, but it'll buy me four minutes."
text_by_relation.known: "Back again." He almost smiles. "Grab a crate, don't sit on the cable."

runs.text: "I do." No heat in it at all. "He talks. I book the slot, I fix the feed, I keep the licence, and I sit in the corner making sure the thing that goes out is a thing and not a man shouting in a basement." A beat. "Some weeks the difference is thin."

satinit.text: Phil is quiet for a second. "He never treated it as a set," he says. "Not once, in nineteen weeks. He'd come in, take his coat off, put it over the back of the chair like he was home." He squares the clipboard against his chest. "You can decide for yourself what it means that I let him keep doing that. I have decided several things and none of them stayed decided."

options.label: And Nguyen sat in it every week.

theset.text: "Down to the pull-string on the bulb," Phil says, and for the first time there's something like pride in it. "Neil described it once, at four in the morning, for about ninety minutes. I had it built. The laundromat overhead is a sound cue and we recorded it in the actual street, because he said it wouldn't be right otherwise." He looks at the corner where the stool is. "It's the best thing I have ever made and I don't think one viewer has ever noticed it's a room."
